newsitem.title: INDIA: India Kinetic delays China joint venture.
newsitem.headline: India Kinetic delays China joint venture.

text.p: India scooter-maker Kinetic Engineering Ltd has placed its proposed joint venture to manufacture scooter engines in China on hold for about a year, a company official said.
"There is right now a big glut in China," Kinetic chairman Arun Firodia told Reuters in an interview at his headquarters in the western city of Pune.

Kinetic had planned to make 100,000 engines per annum of 50 cc to 70 cc capacity in a one-million-rupee joint venture with a Chinese partner, he said, but had decided to wait until the glut was exhausted.
"There is overcapacity. And the Chinese economy is expanding fast. Still there is overcapacity. So our would-be partner said 'Let's wait'. After a year we will begin operations."
He declined to give the name of the Chinese partner.
Industry analysts estimate that China's nine-million strong market for two-wheelers will grow to 10 million by the end of the financial year.

"The market size is now about nine million in China, and we expect it to grow to about 10 million by the end of the year," Hideo Tanaka, managing director of Kinetic Honda Motor Ltd, estimated recently.
Kinetic has a 27 percent share of India's low-power two-wheeler market, dominated by TVS Suzuki Ltd and Majestic Auto Ltd.
Kinetic showed net profits of 134.8 million rupees in 1996/97 (April-March), 2.7 percent down from 138.5 million rupees the previous year.
